summary_en: This phase 2 study tests the combination of epcoritamab and lenalidomide in patients with refractory or relapsed immunodeficiency-related large B-cell lymphoma. Epcoritamab is given under the skin (subcutaneous) weekly during cycle 1, then on days 1, 8, 15 and 22 of cycles 2-3, and on day 1 of cycles 4-12. Lenalidomide is taken by mouth on days 1-21 of each 28-day cycle, for up to 12 months if the disease does not progress and side effects are manageable. The main outcome measure is not stated in the record; the study is a phase 2 trial.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa la combinación de epcoritamab y lenalidomida en pacientes con linfoma de células B grandes relacionado con inmunodeficiencia, refractario o recidivante. El epcoritamab se administra por vía subcutánea una vez por semana durante el ciclo 1, luego los días 1, 8, 15 y 22 de los ciclos 2-3, y el día 1 de los ciclos 4-12. La lenalidomida se toma por vía oral los días 1-21 de cada ciclo de 28 días, durante hasta 12 meses si la enfermedad no progresa y los efectos secundarios son manejables. El registro no indica el resultado principal que se mide; el estudio es de fase 2.
who_for: Confirmed immunodeficiency-related large B-cell lymphoma, including monomorphic post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder or certain polymorphic B-cell disor
Disease that did not respond well to first-line chemo-immunotherapy or rituximab, or that came back after a complete response.
Judged ineligible for CAR-T cell therapy.
At least one measurable lesion on CT or MRI under Lugano criteria.
Age 18 or older with ECOG performance status 0-2.
not_for: Prior therapy with a bispecific T-cell engager targeting CD3 and CD20.
Chemotherapy or other antineoplastic therapy within about 1 week, or autologous stem cell transplant within 100 days.
Active disease in the central nervous system or uncontrolled seizures.
Myocardial infarction or stroke within 6 months, or left ventricular ejection fraction below 45%.
Pregnancy or breastfeeding, or live vaccine within 30 days before the first dose.
